ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Shuffle the item-to-row association of the cached incoming-context signal before training, keeping edge weights, codebook, Sinkhorn, and all hyperparameters unchanged.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use correctly aligned training-only incoming-context signal and Poincare distances in the assignment pathway.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace every d_c^2 in assignment cost by squared Euclidean distance and exp/projection by identity, with same behavior, weights, temperature, and sparse Sinkhorn.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the frozen training split only, count adjacent item transitions p->i, deduplicate per user-session, downweight predecessor p by 1/sqrt(1+training_item_frequency(p)); build P(i) and cache sparse edges once. No re-sampling or split mixing.
ideas.behavior_signal: Training-only directed sequential co-consumption predecessor-to-target edges and the target's incoming predecessor-region mixture.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time sparse edge aggregation O(E_train); per step for batch B, K codewords and top-32 mask, O(B*32*d + B*32*3) distances/normalization, versus dense O(B*K*d); expected <5% step overhead after edge gather/cache. At frozen scale 24,556 items x 24 steps x 3,000 epochs = 72,000 steps, about 1.77 billion sparse assignment-distance evaluations at B~items/24, plus the baseline RQ-VAE cost.
ideas.coupling_equation: A_i=SparseSinkhorn(exp(-[(1-lambda_i)d_c(x_i,c_k)^2 + lambda_i d_c(q_i,c_k)^2]/tau)); q_i=Proj(sum_{p->i}w_pi sum_k a_pk c_k/sum_{p->i}w_pi). The behaviour term q_i and curved term d_c jointly set A_i.
ideas.coupling_path: Training predecessor edges -> soft predecessor code mixture -> projected curved context q_i -> curved context-plus-content assignment cost -> Sinkhorn/hard token. Removing edges eliminates q_i; replacing d_c with Euclidean distance changes both context and content assignment geometry.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Items with several distinct incoming contexts are the difficult targets; the adaptive curved context term should reduce their cross-region assignment dispersion and improve held-out discrimination, raising Stage3 test_R@10 above 0.065. Keep only if L1 Hard ER and the held-out positive-minus-hard-negative gap improve without reducing gold-prefix survival.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside each level's code assignment cost and sparse Sinkhorn logits; it determines the assignments, not a penalty added after quantization.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Squared Poincare geodesic distance d_c^2 at fixed negative curvature -c, c=1, with exp_0 and ball projection for latent/prototype vectors.
ideas.key_change: At each quantizer level, form a target context point from the current soft assignments of its training predecessors, and use that point to tilt the item's Poincare-distance assignment logits before a small sparse Sinkhorn normalization. specification.text: Freeze train co-consumption cosine matrix S from training-only user-item rows. For source prefix point r_u=Proj(sum_{l<3} c_{u_l}), define query q_u=Log_0(r_u), map each candidate item latent z_v to y_v=exp_0(z_v), and score s(u,v)=-d_c(r_u,y_v)^2. Combine with reconstruction; its normalized coefficient is alpha=0.1*stopgrad(recon_ema/(loss_ema+eps)), so its initial scale is approximately 1e-5 to 1e-4. Straight-through reassign the target's final-level token to the codeword minimizing d_c(y_i,c_k)^2 - gamma*(s(u,i)-mean_n s(u,n)) differentiable score contribution.

ideas.hyperbolic_location: First-level code candidate score and soft assignment in Stage2; the incoming-context barycenter and negative-context barycenter are directly compared to candidate prototypes before argmin/softmax.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare Frechet/Karcher weighted barycenter and squared Poincare geodesic distance at fixed curvature -0.1; barycenter iterations use log maps to the current iterate and exp map back.
ideas.key_change: Precompute each item's sparse predecessor-region distribution from training transitions, represent the distribution by a weighted Poincare Fréchet barycenter of predecessor first-token prototypes, and include positive-versus-hard-negative geodesic contrast in the first-token candidate score. Optimize sampled candidate comparisons only; no new extension tokens.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Use only training users/events and training timestamps when building n and co-consumption; no validation/test interactions, future events, or prediction-time context enter barycenters or SIDs. Current predecessor assignments are model states trained only on those frozen edges.
ideas.motivation: A next item reached from many distinct prior regions is difficult to tokenize; its first-level region should inherit the concentrated incoming context that best explains its observed predecessors, without collapsing merely similar but behaviorally wrong items together.
ideas.novelty: Use each candidate first-token prototype as a hyperbolic destination and a train-only incoming predecessor-context barycenter as its target, while a co-consumption-hard negative destination supplies explicit rejection pressure. This is not a successor-consensus term added to Euclidean assignment: predecessor concentration and the negative contrast jointly alter the actual curved candidate assignment score.
ideas.observables: Expect target assignment concentration by incoming-region entropy bin, higher positive-minus-negative gap, improved cooccur_overlap_L3 and adjacency_L3, and changes in L1 Hard ER and gold-prefix survival depths 1-4. Report extension alphabet and frozen Stage3 test_R@10 alongside all required measures.
risks: Early assignments make predecessor regions noisy; cached barycenters can stale; entropy gating can suppress useful learning for rare items; incoming context may not align with next-item ranking, and hard negatives can include unobserved transitions.
ideas.safeguards: Smooth incoming counts; fall back to encoder point for no predecessors; renormalize top-M weights; clamp ball norms below (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c), stable log/exp maps and float32, stop gradients through stale cached context, refresh cache once per epoch, mask invalid negatives and skip empty cases. Clip gradients and bound eta/g_i to [0,1]. Keep all sparse data structures train-only; never materialize dense item-item matrices.
ideas.spec_equations: p_i(p)=n_{pi}/(sum_q n_{qi}+eps); q_p(k)=softmax(-d_c(v_k,z_p)^2/tau_q); r_i(k)=sum_p p_i(p)*stopgrad(q_p(k)); H_i=-sum_k r_i(k)log(r_i(k)+eps)/log(max(2,K)); g_i=clip(1-H_i,0,1). For top M=8 predecessors, b_i initialized at highest-weight prototype and repeat 8 times: u=sum_p p_i(p)log_{b}(v_{a_p}); b=exp_b(u), renormalizing weights over retained predecessors. Select r(i)=argmax cooc_cos(i,r) subject to no train edge r->i. Compute S(i,k) as in COUPLING EQUATION; q_i=softmax(-S(i,:)/tau), use straight-through argmax; add standard RQ-VAE reconstruction and commitment/codebook losses. Compute negative b_r identically. A detach assignment probabilities in barycenter construction each epoch; gradients flow through candidate distances and assignment only.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are train-only sparse directed transition counts, train co-consumption nearest-neighbor lists, item IDs, first-token prototypes/assignments, encoder latents, c=-0.1, M=8, Karcher iterations=8, eta and temperature. Outputs are per-item cached behavior barycenters/gates, first-token candidate scores/probabilities, and unchanged downstream residual tokens.

specification.text: Build directed counts n_{pi} from adjacent training events. During a minibatch, get the current soft first-token probabilities q_p over K prototypes and compute for target i a cached sparse weighted prototype barycenter b_i=FrechetMean_{p:n_pi>0}(prototype[p], normalized n_pi). For each target, select positive target-side context i and hard negative item r with high training co-consumption cosine but no transition into i. Score candidate code k by S(i,k)=d_c(v_k,b_i)^2 - eta*d_c(v_k,b_r)^2, where b_r is r's incoming-context barycenter; use softmax(-S/tau) for straight-through assignment, plus standard reconstruction/VQ losses. Downweight targets with diffuse predecessor-region distribution using g_i=1-H(p(region|i))/log(max(2,K)), clipped [0,1], so the actual score is S_g=g_i*S+(1-g_i)*S_base-curved; compute g from train counts and current predecessor assignments detached. Curved distance and behavior both enter each candidate score.

objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

## What the measurements on 67 existing SID tables say

Every number below is measured on the same 67 SID tables, each paired with one Stage 3 run
(57,439 test rows) and joined on the SID's sha256, not on the arm name (the 67 tables carry
only 53 distinct names).

1. **Co-occurrence coherence inside the three-token prefix is the strongest target.**
   `cooccur_overlap_L3` = the mean cosine similarity of the training co-consumption rows of
   item pairs that share a three-token prefix. Spearman 0.902 [0.831, 0.939] with
   `test_recall@10`; out-of-sample R2 0.705 against 0.554 for a straight line (isotonic wins
   20 of 20 repeats, paired +0.151 [+0.126, +0.175]). The random-pair baseline of that
   similarity is 0.0269, so the raw value is `lift x 0.0269`.
2. **It is monotone but saturating.** Quintile means of the metric against mean recall:
   0.0503 -> 0.0472, 0.0721 -> 0.0552, 0.0907 -> 0.0572, 0.1125 -> 0.0601,
   0.1527 -> 0.0623. The first step buys 0.0080 of recall for 0.022 of metric, the last buys
   0.0022 for 0.040. There is a step at 0.0585 worth +0.0120 recall (permutation p = 0.0005).
   The best table in the sample is 0.0643 at 0.168, so beating 0.065 needs to go past the best
   observed coherence, not towards it.
3. **Discrimination beats similarity, and the negative side is the informative half.** On the
   canonical held-out pairs (52,855 validity pairs, ten fixed negatives each), scoring by the
   co-occurrence cosine gives: the positive-only similarity correlates +0.229 (p = 0.068) with
   recall, the positive-minus-negative gap correlates **+0.877** (p = 0.0003), and the negative
   similarity alone **-0.720**. Two tables can have equally similar positives and differ
   completely in how hard their negatives sit next to the region. This gap keeps +0.431 of
   partial correlation after controlling for `cooccur_overlap_L3`.
4. **Concentrated incoming context is the positive property.** For every target item, the
   distinct L1 regions among its training predecessors, divided by its distinct predecessors:
   the raw correlation flips sign with the region depth (+0.333 at L3, -0.292 at L1) because the
   L3 measure saturates, but after controlling for the table's granularity the relation is
   negative at every depth (-0.574 to -0.658). A target reached from many different regions is
   the hard one.
5. **Two controls carry no information and one is harmful.** `L1_distinct` (rho -0.199,
   p = 0.117) and `L1_code_entropy_bits` (-0.035) do not predict recall; `ext_distinct`, the
   width of the collision-extension alphabet, is **-0.471**. Successor-side coherence
   (`adjacency_L1/L2/L3` 0.820-0.825, `succ_overlap_within_L1` 0.847) and held-out prefix
   discrimination (`er_l1/l2/l3` 0.759-0.782) are the other two correlated families.
6. **What the current mechanisms achieve.** The best arms in the sample come from a behaviour
   transition pipeline with per-epoch pair resampling (0.0624-0.0643). Every arm built on this
   repository's frozen RQ-VAE baseline with a behaviour-shaped loss lands at 0.0506-0.0559.
   The Stage 3 target is `test_recall@10 > 0.065`.

## What this round must design

A mechanism whose **behaviour signal** is train-only co-consumption and whose **curve
arithmetic** is explicit, coupled on one connected computational path, in the sense of the
scope contract. The measurements point at three design elements, and a proposal must use at
least two of them on the same path:

* the objective should be a **discrimination** rather than a similarity: the same batch-level
  geometry should pull the co-occurrence profile of a region towards what actually follows and
  push it away from the items that are co-occurrence-close but do not follow (hard negatives
  chosen by co-occurrence similarity, not at random);
* the region of an item must **inherit the incoming context** rather than only its own
  embedding: items whose training predecessors arrive from several regions should be pulled
  together, which is a constraint on the assignment and therefore on the codebook geometry;
* the curved operation must be the one that computes the assignment or the contrast, not a
  post-hoc penalty on finished codes, and the extension alphabet must not grow.

## Requirements

* the behaviour signal is built once from the training split and frozen; no validation or test
  behaviour, no future information, no user context at prediction time;
* the ablated controls are mandatory: behaviour-off (shuffle the item-to-row association of the
  signal) and geometry-off (Euclidean in the same place, same weights);
* the term must be scale-matched against the reconstruction loss (which is ~1e-4) and must stay
  sparse per step;
* report `L1 Hard ER`, `cooccur_overlap_L3` (the target), `adjacency_L3`, the
  positive-minus-negative gap, gold-prefix survival at depths 1-4, the extension alphabet, and
  Stage 3 `test_R@10`.

## Frozen constraints

Four tokens, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, no early stopping, no test-time tuning, the
frozen Stage 3 protocol, the baseline tree is the one the scope contract names.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. The HGCN vector quantizes the SURF feature space, leading to a bag-of-word (BoW) representation construction of the images. This representation is subsequently used to determine LCD accuracy and recall. Our approaches in this study are referred to as HGCN-FABMAP and HGCN-ORB. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. In the backward pass, a discounted Hyperbolic Straight-Through Estimator routes the reconstruction gradient through the quantizer as a single geometric block, avoiding unstable recursive gradient transport across residual stages. papers.title: Geometry-Aware Hyperbolic Residual-Quantized Variational Autoencoders

papers.abstract: We develop a cannonical quantization for massive vector fields on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold.
papers.title: Quantization of massive vector fields in curved space–time

papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. The design of block encoders, under the strong hardware constraints that derive from the A/D converter removal, has been investigated in this paper. We present a comparison of three systems in terms of rate, distortion and complexity, and present a numerical simulation analysis of their sensitivity to implementation errors. The conclusion of the analysis is that linear-transform coding vector quantizers outperform full-search vector quantizers and warping hyperbolic-tangent neural networks, in terms of performance, complexity and robustness, for a CMOS imaging sensor implemen
papers.title: Sensitivity analysis of low-complexity vector quantizers for focal-plane image compression

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. Specifically, the vector quantization error is replaced by product of the original error and a normalized noise vector, the samples of which are drawn from a zero-mean, unit-varianc
papers.title: NSVQ: Noise Substitution in Vector Quantization for Machine Learning

papers.abstract: We establish stable quantum ergodicity for spin Hamiltonians, also known as Pauli-Schrödinger operators. Our approach combines new analytic techniques of mixed quantization, inspired by local index theory, with stable ergodicity results for partially hyperbolic systems.
